einzeiler: House blocks Pete Hegseth impeachment, Jim Jordan chosen as leader, DOJ charges terror…
kurzfassung: House Republicans blocked an impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and elected Jim Jordan as their new leader. Meanwhile, the Department of Justice charged three Iran-backed operatives in connection with numerous terror plots across Europe and the United States. Additionally, a U.S. soldier was arrested in Britain on suspicion of spying for Russia.
stichpunkte: House Republicans used a parliamentary maneuver to block an impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan was chosen as the new top Republican leader in the House, replacing Mike Johnson.
Senate Republicans reelected John Thune as majority leader.
The DOJ indicted three Iran-backed operatives for planning nearly 20 terror plots across Europe and the U.S.
The terror plots included an attempt targeting a British airbase housing American troops.
Federal prosecutors stated that one of the accused men helped coordinate a plot while already in federal custody in New York.
A 41-year-old U.S. soldier was arrested in Britain on suspicion of spying for Russia.

clips.text: The legislative process used to stall the impeachment resolution is compared to being stuck on an indefinite customer service phone queue.

clips.hook: Light it up like a Christmas tree
clips.text: One of the defendants allegedly instructed an attacker targeting a London synagogue using this phrase.

clips.hook: Insider threats are real and persistent
clips.text: A military official described the arrest of a senior soldier suspected of espionage as a stark warning about security vulnerabilities.

beschreibung:
House Republicans blocked an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, but lawmakers still have other ways to challenge the administration over the Iran war and its push for more defense spending.
House Republicans chose Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan to lead them in the minority, signaling a more combative approach as the party prepares to face a Democratic majority next year.
Federal prosecutors say three Iran-backed operatives were involved in nearly twenty attacks or attempted attacks across Europe and the United States, while a separate case involving a U.S. soldier accused of spying for Russia is raising new security concerns in Britain.
